body.x: UNIUNI, a startup specializing in privacy-preserving AI technology, announced that its home safety solution, SAVVY SPACE AI, won a Best of Innovation Award in the Smart Home category at CES 2027. Building on its experience developing privacy-preserving systems that detect illegal filming and safety risks in public restrooms, UNIUNI has expanded the technology into home safety applications.

SAVVY SPACE AI is a home solution that applies Savvy Modular AI, which lets the safety functions a space needs be configured as required. Through the product, UNIUNI presented its vision of "Privacy-Preserving Safety for Every Space."

UNIUNI's savvy1.5, an always-on AI system designed to detect suspected illegal filming and safety emergencies in public restrooms, monitors potential threats, including suspicious radio-frequency signals, while preserving users' privacy and enabling facility managers to respond even when inspection staff are not on site.

The technology began with the question of how privacy and safety can coexist. UNIUNI developed Non-Vision AI, which analyzes non-identifying sensor data, such as distance measurements, without relying on conventional camera footage. In public restrooms, it uses this to detect suspected illegal filming and risk signals such as falls that facility managers need to check.

UNIUNI won an Innovation Award in the Smart Communities category at CES 2025 for the accessible-restroom safety solution "SAVVY Accessible Restroom: Privacy for Differently Abled." At CES 2026, it received awards in two categories — Products in Support of Human Security for All and Smart Communities — for the public-restroom safety solution "Restroomguard Savvy: Privacy-First Community Security AI." The company has continued releasing products that detect suspected illegal filming, falls, screams and other risk signals in public spaces where privacy matters, focusing on public safety.

The 2027 Best of Innovation was awarded to SAVVY SPACE AI in the Smart Home field. At home, the bathroom, bedroom and living room each carry different lifestyles and safety concerns: bathrooms call for guarding against slips and falls, while in a bedroom or living room a person living alone who collapses may find it hard to call for help nearby. Bathrooms and bedrooms in particular must be watched for safety while carefully protecting residents' privacy.

Designed with this in mind, SAVVY SPACE AI detects risks such as falls without ordinary camera video that captures faces or indoor scenes. SAVVY SPACE AI is a product-design approach that configures sensors and AI functions to match a space's purpose and the detection it requires. On this basis, UNIUNI plans to apply the safety functions each space needs within the home and to broaden its reach to various living spaces such as care facilities.

"Operating technology that continuously detects illegal filming and various risks in public restrooms — multi-use facilities rich in diverse data — we have developed technology that saves lives while protecting users' privacy," said Sooyeon Han, CEO of UNIUNI. "I want to extend that experience to the home, where people stay even longer than in restrooms and risks grow, to save more lives." She added, "Every space where people stay must be safe, and that technology must always respect human rights."

UNIUNI has a track record of installing its always-on illegal-filming detection and fall- and risk-detection AI at more than 1,100 public facilities in Korea, where it has detected some 160 incidents and saved real lives, and it plans to expand into care facilities, homes and more.
